title: Email and newsletter monitoring intake
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor or user, I want email/newsletter sources to enter common Monitoring intake with correct provenance and privacy, so that useful content can be evaluated alongside other discoveries.

New feature planning. User correction is authoritative for capability scope: Papyrus must NOT be represented as already having working inbound email monitors. Existing outbound SES, security or submission-related source artifacts are not proof of a shipped inbound-monitoring capability or any current deployment. No extended email audit is needed in this filing; any reusable components must be verified by the implementation owner later without assuming readiness.

Design options: (1) an external IMAP/POP3 mailbox with a read-only connection and no mailbox mutation; (2) a Papyrus-provided SES inbound address scoped to the authorized publication/user for newsletters and editorial submissions. Preserve these as options until platform capability, address routing, sender policy, reader permissions, authentication/credential storage, privacy/retention/deletion, consent, costs and operational ownership are decided. No mailbox connection, MX/DNS/receipt-rule changes, address provisioning, newsletter subscription, purchase, credential handling or model call now.

Both options feed existing common intake rather than a second research engine. Extract useful editorial content links and body text, retain message/source/publication/user provenance, deduplicate replays and tracking variants without discarding meaningful updates, treat all message contents as untrusted, and distinguish editorial links from unsubscribe/preferences/login/magic-token actions or secret-bearing URLs. Do not follow action links or leak credentials/tokens into References, classifier inputs, logs or public outputs. Resolve publication/user routing and access before intake.

Separate related milestone to general Monitoring PPY-2d77c8, not under Markus for everything and not a prerequisite for the first recurring 3–5 source feed/crawler slice. Initial consumer interest includes academic Papyrus, Threat Intelligence and Anth.us through common configuration. Implementation remains unstarted.

Provided-address email monitoring requires a usable human newsletter inbox/reader, not only hidden ingestion. Behavior PPY-7a2a53d7-0e93-4ee9-b8c3-732125a86537 covers readable originals, sender/date, derived-reference provenance, processing status/errors and deliberate human confirmation/unsubscribe actions. Scanners never activate account-action links. Pausing a Monitor is not unsubscribe. Full compose/reply mail client remains out of scope. Documentation behavior PPY-d97519f8-a11e-4501-a558-8be1027e9f2a and dependent acceptance review PPY-33aeaffa-2883-4b5f-99df-937f5110c378 are part of this milestone. No email action or connection now.

User-initiated unsubscribe acceptance is owned by PPY-bfcc3231-eceb-4b90-8d9b-de9990726b2e. A usable reader offers an explicitly clicked automated RFC 8058 HTTPS one-click flow where the message/header authentication and target requirements are met; it shows request/result/error status without claiming sender delivery has stopped. Without supported authenticated one-click, offer an appropriate external unsubscribe page for deliberate user action. Mailto-only limited outbound remains a design question, not a full mail client. Ingestion/link scanning never confirms or unsubscribes automatically; pause is not unsubscribe. This refines the earlier “manual management” wording: consent is manual, while a supported request may be automated after the user's click. Source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8058 .

LATEST first milestone and implementation scope: real recurring Monitor -> persisted deduplicated References and provenance -> the correct publication's REAL Cyclotron prediction -> human review in the EXISTING curation UI -> an authorized human label under current authority rules -> verified applied steering/training receipt. Predictions, agent judgments and advisory feedback never count as human labels. Recorded, queued and applied feedback are distinct; claim training/optimization only with an applied receipt, never from prediction alone. Respect existing proof/authorization gates; do not bypass them to manufacture a receipt.

One configured Monitor per initial publication is sufficient. Start with 1–2 source adapters: Hacker News first, then a verified current Hugging Face paper/academic source only as a useful bounded increment. Initial consumers are Anth.us, the academic Papyrus publication and Threat Intelligence; exact source-to-publication mapping is flexible and one upstream source may serve multiple independently scoped classifiers. Verify current application/binding ownership and guidance; never assume legacy dbsyytcm9drqa. Pilobolus is not an initial target because its serendipitous content is harder to monitor, not because it is permanently excluded. Preserve recurring, source-appropriate cadence around 15 minutes, checkpoints, dedup/new/updated items, provenance and visible stage failures so relevant discoveries and the learning loop are available for morning review.

Rich Monitoring UI/new inbox, email/unsubscribe, expensive LLM section/desk triage and Markus for everything are MUCH LOWER priority and MUST NOT block this slice. Use existing capabilities and curation UI; choose the operator/configuration interface during implementation, with no required new configuration UI. Additional adapters, 3–5 source expansion and richer views are later increments. Reuse current scheduling/intake/classification/label paths and coordinate intake PR367 instead of duplicating it.

Ryan explicitly authorized implementation of THIS first slice after filing, with public-source intake/classification needed for it. That does not authorize production merge/deployment, new persistent access/IAM, purchases, mailbox/MX changes, subscriptions, AWS-console browser work or unrelated benchmarks. No fabricated human labels. Other new feature plans remain unstarted.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Planning delivery on develop: new email/newsletter monitoring milestone with read-only IMAP/POP3 and provided SES-address design options; no existing inbound-monitor capability claimed. Required reader PPY-7a2a53 supports original messages, sender/date, reference provenance and processing status/errors. Explicitly clicked RFC8058 request behavior PPY-bfcc32 requires authenticated supported headers/HTTPS, truthful request/result status and external fallback; no delivery-stop guarantee, automatic ingestion actions or full compose/reply client. Docs PPY-d97519 and review PPY-33aeaf are linked; provided-address behavior depends on reader and review depends on reader/docs/unsubscribe. All remain open and implementation unstarted. Full planning-set readback passed and no new board validation errors. No email, unsubscribe, connection, infrastructure or model action performed.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Codex is implementing the user-authorized 2026-10-23 backend slice in PPY-65026c, branch feature/PPY-65026c-email-submissions, isolated worktree based on origin/develop 79bee759. Existing inbox/reader/unsubscribe plans remain separate. No Claude work changed. Plan: explicit publication/shared address bindings; authenticated bounded MIME/link intake through Monitoring and pending References; no console-agent execution; cloud email independent of newsletter. IaC and local fixtures only; no live AWS or email.
